title: Reuters: some IPO investors see $1.5 trillion as the high end
friendlyTitle: Reuters: some investors think $1.5 trillion is too high for Anthropic
summary: On 5 November, Reuters reported that potential investors are raising doubts about whether Anthropic can start its planned IPO roadshow next week and still list in November. Four people familiar with the discussions said some investors view a recently discussed $1.5 trillion valuation as the high end, and that Anthropic may need a larger discount to secure commitments. They pointed to quarterly losses and large spending commitments. Two of the people said investors are also waiting on the October revenue figure, which was left blank in the updated S-1 filing. Reuters previously reported that the roadshow had been expected to start the week of 9 November, with pricing the following week. Earlier this year, some investors had expected a valuation as high as $2 trillion. Reuters says some people familiar with the talks expect the offering itself to reach as much as $100 billion, and that a weak market for AI stocks could lead the company to wait. Anthropic declined to comment. Reuters also notes a Wall Street Journal report, on Thursday evening, that IPO investors are skeptical of the $1.5 trillion figure. This is not a cancelled listing. It is a report that the price and the date are both under pressure.
friendlySummary: On 5 November, Reuters reported that some possible investors doubt Anthropic can start its stock-sale tour next week and still list in November. An IPO is the first sale of a company's shares to the public. A roadshow is the set of meetings where the company asks investors to commit. Four people familiar with the talks said some investors see a recently discussed $1.5 trillion company value as the high end, and that Anthropic may need a bigger discount to get them to sign. They pointed to quarterly losses and large spending promises. Two of the people said investors are also waiting for the October revenue number, which was left blank in the updated filing. Reuters had earlier reported that the tour was expected to start the week of 9 November, with the price set the week after. Earlier this year, some investors had talked about a value as high as $2 trillion. Reuters says some people close to the talks expect the share sale itself to be as large as $100 billion, and that a weak market could make the company wait. Anthropic declined to comment. Reuters also notes a Wall Street Journal report, on Thursday evening, that investors are skeptical of the $1.5 trillion figure. This is not a cancelled sale. It is a report that the price and the date are both under pressure.
whyItMatters: If you pay Anthropic by the month, this does not change your invoice. It does change the story that the next price rise is inevitable because the stock sale is already priced. The blank October revenue line is the number the buyers say they are waiting on. Until Anthropic fills it in, a valuation quote is a negotiation, not a result.
